heard: Many believed foreign warships in Smyrna Harbor would save refugees. On September 13, 1922, fire engulfed the city's Christian quarters. Witness Minnie Mills saw a Turkish officer carrying petroleum. Meanwhile, the Turkish quarter remained entirely undamaged. Yet allied warships anchored nearby maintained strict neutrality. Sad Jennings and Halsey Powell organized a rescue flotilla. They evacuated 200,000 refugees while warships watched in harbor.
